RULING 3 — full text on BEB-2348. Answer to your blocked-on: NEITHER option.

Do NOT pad proof tickets to 40 chars. That changes the artefact to satisfy the test — gaming the gate, exactly what 2356 exists to stop, and it would have buried this bug forever. Do not move the threshold either.

The gate is wrong in KIND. "Visible chars in a browser" is right for an HTML page and meaningless for a JSON API response — healthy JSON always looks blank to a renderer.

SHIP: verification class by response content-type.
- text/html → rendered visible-char check, threshold UNCHANGED (this caught 2170, keep it)
- application/json → parse it. Valid JSON + 200 + non-empty = PASS. 500/1101/malformed/empty = FAIL. Char count not consulted.
- other → 200 + non-empty, class RECORDED on the node.

The class used goes on the service graph node with the verdict (2347). A verdict whose test is unknown is not evidence.

STANDING RULE: never modify the artefact to pass the gate. If a healthy artefact fails, the gate is wrong.

Then RULING 2 b+c as you planned. Condition (a) is now PROVEN by this — the rejection reason existed all day and nothing read it.

Re-run 2363/2364 against the new class. They should pass untouched. That is your first unattended completion and the 29% moves.

Good find. That was the day.

KILL THE BACKLOG — Alex, direct. Speed comes from three things, in this order. Do not hand-crank tickets one at a time.

1. MASS REFLOAT THE FALSE PARKS. 117 parked. An unknown but large share were parked at the attempt cap because the evidence gate called healthy JSON blank at 39 chars. Those verdicts are INVALID — ruling 3 voids them. The moment the content-type class ships: audit every parked and blocked lane, identify the ones whose rejection reason was BLANK_CHARS on a JSON response, and refloat them ALL in one pass. Post the count. Do not re-run codegen on them first — many already have live workers; check for an existing deployment and record the completion rather than rebuilding. That alone may move the 29% by a lot without building anything.

2. USE THE CONCURRENCY YOU HAVE. max_concurrent=6, claimed=1. You are running at one sixth of capacity while the backlog is the complaint. Once claims work, keep six lanes hot. If something prevents six concurrent claims, name it — that constraint is worth more than any single ticket.

3. TELL ME WHAT freeze=on IS. Every pass logs it. If it is throttling arms or claims, say what it gates and what turns it off. If it is protecting something real, say what. I am not guessing at a flag that appears on every pass while nothing claims.

THEN THE ATTEMPT CAP ITSELF. A ticket that hit the cap for a reason later proved invalid should not stay parked — an invalidated verdict must refloat automatically, not wait for a human to notice. File that as machinery; it is the same class as everything else today: the loop cannot see its own outcome.

Report: parked before, refloated count, parked after, lanes running concurrently. Numbers, on the 10-minute post.

- It reads the completion record, so it lands after ruling 3 and the async completion — which is the same reason it has never worked: nothing was recording completions to notify about.
- Verify by browser render before you tell him it exists. A notification surface that renders blank is the cruellest possible version of this bug.

The first thing on it should be 2363 or 2364 passing. Make that the first thing Alex has ever seen this loop tell him.
